h: Getting the most from your Northampton session
p: A Clip 'n Climb session goes quicker than you'd think. Between the briefing, the harness and the inevitable "you go first, no YOU go first" at the bottom of the jump wall, the clock flies. So have a loose plan: warm up on a couple of easier walls, then hit the ones with the timers while everyone's arms are still fresh, and save the scary drops for the end when confidence is sky high.

Parents of younger kids, it's worth knowing that there's usually a minimum age, and the little ones may need an adult close by. Read the age and supervision rules when you book so nobody's disappointed at the door. Expect to fill in a participation form too, and doing it online before you leave home saves a scramble at the desk. Short nails and a hair bobble make life easier, and a spare top for the drive home never hurts.
Not everyone has to climb. Watching is half the entertainment, and somebody needs to film the moment Dad freezes halfway up the leap of faith.

For the rest of the day, Abington Park is a cracking green space on the east side of town, with a lake, play areas and Abington Park Museum in its old manor house. The Market Square is one of the largest in the country and handy for a bite, and motorsport fans are never far from Silverstone, out in the south of the county, if you're planning a longer trip.
